utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We've got a couple of minutes before we are due to break. Just want to deal with this one important housekeeping matter. This very witness who has just stood down once again has gone far beyond the time allocated to him, and at this rate I don't see how we are going to keep within the time-limits. And I just want to say to the parties that the Chamber wants to warn you now that it is going to adhere very strictly to the time-limits. The Chamber is mindful of the fact that the Defence has submitted further 65 ter estimates, and in the light of that, the Chamber is going to give you a revised 73 ter decision regulating the number of hours and we are going to have to deal -- stick to those hours. Mr. Milovancevic, earlier you said you didn't understand what I meant by one-third time. What I wanted to say about that time was, having realised that trying to divide the time on a 50/50 basis between the Defence and the Prosecution, this obviously leaves us no time for questions by the Bench and questions for re-examination by the Defence. The Bench is now going to insist that when a third of your time is over you stop leading, and the Prosecution must try to cross-examine within the next third, and the last third of the time is going to be used for re-examination and questions by the Bench. That's how we are going to regulate the time. You're going to have to, both of you, all of us, are going to have to learn to economise with time and put very succinct questions to the witness and control the witness to give us succinct and pertinent answers without any frills attached to the answer. So that's how we are going to do it. As soon as the 73 ter decision is out, we are going to go by that estimation. For the time being, we shall go by the estimation that was given by the Defence before -- the latest 65 ter estimation. Yes, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to explain something. The Defence is aware that we have overstepped some lines, as far as the allowed time for examination is concerned. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: (redacted) -- they are telling me that I'm speaking too fast. Maybe, in fact, we believe that we discussed very important relevant matters with these witnesses. And another point I wish to make is that we do know we have a certain time allowed for presenting our case, and we do not intend, I'm saying this with full responsibility, to ask for an extension just because we spent more or less time with one of the witnesses. That is not our intent and not our plan, and we know that the Trial Chamber would not grant us that extension, even if we were to ask for it. I know. Maybe I mentioned -- maybe this calls for a small redaction because I mentioned some of the offices held by prior witnesses. I didn't mention their names but maybe -- maybe we still need to redact that part of the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But let me say something, Mr. Milovancevic. You know, I hear what you say that we have got -- we have been having important witnesses coming to testify. The Chamber has concerns about how the Defence has conducted itself in this matter. The Defence, first of all, gave us a 65 ter list based on which the Chamber gave a 73 ter decision, and the Defence has always said it will stay within the time-limit as given in the 73 ter decision. We have not been able to do so. And when the Defence comes and submits its second 65 ter estimate, which came out a couple of days ago, it does not even use the 73 ter decision as a basis. It uses its own original 65 ter and gives us that as a comparison -- tries to show us how it has reduced time from its original list, which list is not working any longer because there is now a decision in place. So the Defence is not showing any inclination to stick to what the Court decides. But that's not all. The second point is -- these are two important points that I want to mention to you -- that as you say to us, these are important witnesses, and this time you are going to catch up with -- as time goes on, you're not telling us how you're going to do that. It's not mentioned in your 65 ter list. It's not mentioned anywhere. So without any indication of how you intend to conduct the Defence case in the future, the Chamber has no choice but to exercise control, and that is the control that we are going to exercise until such time as you have shown -- the Defence has shown how they are going to save on this time. The last point I just want to raise from what you said now is that you know that even if you say you're going to stick to the times put by the Chamber, and you know that even if you asked for the time the Chamber wouldn't give you that, don't prejudge the Bench. The Bench does not prejudge the case. If an application comes, the Bench will look at it on its merits and will decide accordingly. It's not for you to say this Bench will not grant you an application when you make one in the future. I think that is not appropriate. And I don't think there is any need for us, Mr. Milovancevic, to go into further discussions of this point. I think that the Bench has indicated how it is going to conduct the trial henceforth and you must play your part to convince the Bench that, indeed, we will make up the time. Then the Bench will listen to you at that stage. I don't think -- what did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we now got only one-third of our estimate. The Prosecutor was not subject to such restrictions. As for the last witness, we did ask for an extension even before he began because we knew it was going to be like this, after we had the chance to talk to him here. The witness who just left was an exception to the rule, absolutely. We provided a new estimate and we will try to adhere to it as realistically as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is not your estimate that you must try to add here to. It is the decision of the Court you must try to adhere to. This is the fundamental difference in the attitude of the Defence and what I'm trying to say to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: All right. Now, thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. Court adjourned until tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 6th day of September, 2006, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.52 p.m.,
